summary: Thunderbolt dock: external displays and keyboard not restored after suspend/resume on provisioned Ubuntu workstations
description: Issue summary: Multiple engineers report that after the latest imaging/provisioning cycle, machines connected to corporate Thunderbolt docks fail to restore external displays and USB input devices after suspend/resume. Impact: productivity loss for docked users; machine appears functional but external monitors remain black and external keyboard/mouse unresponsive until dock power-cycle or full reboot. Scope: observed on ~6 users in SRE and Platform teams; reproducible on two model types in lab.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a machine with the current corporate image (ubuntu-22.04 + endpoint-agent v1.8.0).
2) Connect to company-issued Thunderbolt 4 dock (Anker/CalDigit tested). Attach 2 external monitors (DP/HDMI) and USB keyboard + mouse via dock hub.
3) Confirm displays active and input devices responsive. Lock screen and suspend (sudo systemctl suspend) or close lid to trigger suspend.
4) Wake machine. Observe that internal display resumes but external displays remain black and USB input devices are unresponsive. Dock may show power/activity but no video enumerated.
5) Workaround: unplug and replug dock power or reboot the laptop; displays and keyboard/mouse return after cycle.
observed_behavior: After resume, internal laptop display turns on but external monitors stay blank; xrandr shows connectors disconnected. lsusb does not list hub devices until dock power-cycle. dmesg contains thunderbolt and drm errors.
expected_behavior: External displays and USB devices should re-enumerate on resume without requiring a reboot or dock power-cycle.
logs: Mar 10 09:22:11 laptop kernel: thunderbolt 0000:00:14.0: hostbridge: resume failed, error -12
Mar 10 09:22:12 laptop kernel: drm: connector DP-1: lost link, disabling
Mar 10 09:22:13 laptop kernel: usb 1-4: device not accepting address 5, error -71
Mar 10 09:22:14 laptop systemd: Endpoint agent v1.8.0 started: /opt/redwood/endpoint-agent --daemon
investigation_notes: - Reproduced in lab on Dell XPS 15 and ThinkPad X1 with corporate image 2026-03-09 build.
- Not present on older image (2026-02-24) that uses endpoint-agent v1.6.2 and kernel 5.19 -> suggests regression introduced between imaging builds or bundled kernel modules/firmware.
- Kernel version on failing image: 6.2.14-rt. Working image: 5.19.8. Suspect kernel/thunderbolt driver interaction or fw update on dock.
- Endpoint-agent binds to USB power-management rules; verified systemd sleep hooks run but no explicit module reload on resume.
- Quick test: running 'sudo modprobe -r thunderbolt && sudo modprobe thunderbolt' after resume re-enumerates devices without reboot.
- Searched upstream kernel changelogs: several thunderbolt/resume fixes in 6.x series; also known regressions with certain firmware versions on CalDigit TB4 docks.
- Checked corporate Dock firmware: some units running v1.02, others v1.04. v1.04 has reported fixes for Windows only; Linux behavior unclear.
workaround: Power-cycle dock or run 'sudo modprobe -r thunderbolt && sudo modprobe thunderbolt' after resume. As short-term fix, advise affected users to avoid suspend when docked or close lid with external display as internal-only session.
next_steps: 1) Coordinate with SRE to capture serial console + persistent journal on next occurrence and attach full dmesg output.
2) Spin up image with kernel 5.19 (previous working baseline) to confirm regression window and create controlled A/B test.
3) Test latest mainline kernel (6.5 rc) in lab to see if resume regression already fixed upstream.
4) File upstream bug with kernel thundebolt maintainers if reproduction steps confirmed; include dmesg and usb/dp logs.
5) Evaluate rolling back kernel in next imaging build or adding resume-trigger module reload hook in endpoint-agent as a mitigation (requires QA and release plan).
6) Communicate temporary mitigation and instructions to affected teams and update Confluence runbook.
